summary: Akio Tanabe is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1994). He served as an associate professor at Kyoto University (~1998–2009) and held a post at the University of Tokyo (~2017).
Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1935), where he later served as a research group leader (班長).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1954–1975) and later taught at Waseda, Rissho, and other institutions.

Akira Miyaji is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his B.A., M.A., and D.Litt at Nagoya University, where he became emeritus professor, and held posts at Hirosaki University, Ryukoku University, and the Ryukoku Museum.

Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Hokkaido University. He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (attested 1978) and as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine (1929–2018) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1956). He held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, Ryukoku University, and the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism.

Akira Onda (1925–2015) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950), later becoming professor emeritus there (attested 2002). Active in Buddhist studies and other fields, he was a professor at Toyo University (~1965–1996) and taught at Kawamura Gakuen Women's University.

Akira Sadakata is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Akira Hirakawa, and at the University of Paris. He served at Tokai University as associate professor, professor, and emeritus professor.

Akira Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, under Jikido Takasaki, and earned his Ph.D. from the Australian National University. He held professorships at Mie University, the University of Tokyo, and ICPBS.

Akira Shimada specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and completed doctoral studies under Daud Ali, later working at the British Museum and SUNY New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Toyo University. He spent his career at Toyo University as an assistant, associate professor, professor, and president (1991–1994).

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1958). He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1977–1991) and also held posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University and Meikai University.

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying under Akira Hirakawa, Naoshiro Tsuji, J.W. de Jong, and A.L. Basham. He held posts at the Australian National University, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Soka University.
Akitoshi Saito is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at Temple University (attested 1988), he held appointments at the University of Delaware, including professor (1992) and associate professor of philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

Alan Sponberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of British Columbia. He held posts at Princeton University as a professor (attested 1980–1987) and at Stanford University (attested 1988).
Alan Watts (1915–1973) was a writer and thinker in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at St Hugh's School and The King's School, Canterbury (~1928–1932).

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1963–1967) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1967–1973). He held a post at the University of Toronto from ~1973 to 2011.

Alastair Gornall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who received his PhD from the University of Cambridge (~2008–2013). He was an assistant professor at Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2016) and a research associate at SOAS (attested 2019).
